question: According to the ILAE 2015 operational definition, a seizure lasting 5 minutes or more should be treated as status epilepticus (T1 — the time point at which treatment must begin).

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is true. The older teaching that 'status epilepticus = seizure >30 minutes' has been replaced by the ILAE 2015 operational definition: T1 = 5 minutes (treat NOW), T2 = 30 minutes (risk of neuronal damage). A seizure continuing for ≥5 minutes should trigger immediate benzodiazepine administration, because most seizures that do not self-terminate by 5 minutes will not do so spontaneously.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. The ILAE 2015 definition establishes two operational time points: T1 (≥5 minutes) = the time at which a seizure is unlikely to self-terminate and treatment must begin immediately; T2 (≥30 minutes) = the time beyond which there is a risk of long-term neurological damage. Waiting for 30 minutes before treating is dangerous — the 5-minute threshold mandates immediate pharmacological intervention.
